summary: As a WhatsApp automation developer, I feel the pain of dealing with media inconsistencies in unofficial libraries, but I already have workarounds (custom encoding, retries, manual handling). I wouldn't pay much for a dedicated solution because the free libraries and my own code get the job done most of the time. If the official API is acceptable for my use case, I'd switch to that instead. A paid SaaS would need to be extremely easy to integrate, save me significant time, and handle every media type flawlessly for me to consider it.
strongest_points: It could save real development time by removing the need to write and maintain custom media handling code.
If it works with popular libraries (whatsapp-web.js, Baileys) and covers all media types and sizes without failures, it would reduce operational headaches.
For teams building many WhatsApp bots, a reliable media layer might prevent recurring bugs and support requests.
weaknesses: The current workaround (custom code + retries) is workable and costs me nothing, so I'd need a very compelling reason to switch.
My willingness to pay is near zero; I expect free or very cheap because open-source libraries are free and the official API has a low free tier.
I'm skeptical about the reliability and security of a third-party media service that would sit between my bot and WhatsApp; it adds a dependency and potential point of failure.
Integration friction is high: I'd need it to work perfectly with my existing stack and protocol versions, and I'm not sure it would stay up-to-date with WhatsApp changes.
